subject: Dedicated capacity: shoulder/ephemeral carveouts & autoscale policy discussion
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@vistalabs.com>
Cc: VistaLabs Procurement <procurement@vistalabs.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: shoulder/ephemeral carveouts & autoscale policy discussion

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I sketched a conservative capacity and autoscale outline so your platform team can validate against expected traffic patterns next quarter. Key points inline below; attaching a simple diagram and the term sheet draft for visibility.

Proposal (baseline):
- Committed slab: 48 GPUs (pinned for your Dedicated pool)
- Shoulder carveout: 12 GPUs (25% of committed slab) reserved to handle non-deterministic spikes from background batch jobs and sync windows
- Ephemeral buffer pool: 6 GPUs (preemptible) for very short-lived bursts (<= 30 min sustained)

Autoscale & burst policy (SLA-aligned):
- Scale-up ramp: immediate up to 1.5x committed throughput within 2 minutes (will spin ephemeral pool first, then shoulder, then reserved)
- Sustained threshold: any single request pattern sustained > 30 minutes triggers a short review and throttling/crediting dialog (we won't auto-burn shoulder indefinitely)
- Eviction order: ephemeral (preemptible) -> shoulder carveout -> reserved (last resort)
- Cooldown: 10-minute cool-down before scale-down to avoid flapping

Billing/credits for burst:
- Burst credits applied to ephemeral usage first (priced at standard on-demand + 15% premium).
- Shoulder usage billed at committed rate but eligible for monthly reconciliation credits if average utilization of reserved slab remains > 75% for the billing period.

Operational hooks:
- Canary route for model-heavy endpoints to prefer reserved capacity while experimental routes default to shoulder/ephemeral.
- Webhook for VistaLabs SRE when ephemeral pool exceeds 80% so you get advance notice.

Ask from your side: can you confirm the 25/12/6 split maps to your internal spike patterns? Also, please confirm whether you want preemption notifications to go to the SRE pager (we can set a Slack + PagerDuty integration).

Next steps:
1) If that split looks OK, we’ll update the term sheet (attached) with the shoulder carveout language and add the burst credit reconciliation clause.
2) Karthik and Marcus will draft the autoscale policy JSON that your infra team can drop into the cluster config.
3) Procurement can review the term sheet and redlines — Rohan will loop legal once you provide the list of required changes.

Attaching: vista_capacity_diagram.pdf, redwood-dedicated-term-sheet-vl.docx

Thanks,
Rohan

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: shoulder/ephemeral carveouts & autoscale policy discussion

Thanks Rohan — this is really helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 25/12/6 split is a reasonable starting point. Our telemetry team says weekly batch syncs create ~20–25% transient spikes for 15–40 minutes. The ephemeral pool being preemptible is fine.
- We need clearer language on eviction guarantees. For some of our customer-facing models we cannot accept preemption without a graceful fallback (e.g., route to a smaller but warm model). Can you confirm Redwood's fallback behavior when ephemeral is preempted?
- Billing: procurement wants an explicit API for burst usage metrics (per-minute granularity) and a reconciliation example showing how shoulder credits are calculated.

Also: can you add an explicit SLA exception window when we're in a surge and the fallback model reduces quality? We need to capture that in the term sheet so CS can set expectations.

I'll loop in procurement if they want to propose alternative numbering for the buffer pool, but for now the proposed split is workable.

—Asha

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: shoulder/ephemeral carveouts & autoscale policy discussion

Folks — forwarding Asha's questions. I sketched more concrete policy text below that we can convert into the autoscale JSON and add to the term sheet. Marcus, can you validate the fallback ordering and the warm-model routing? Karthik, Ben — please confirm how monthly reconciliation credits should be calculated so we can provide an example table for procurement.

Suggested policy snippets (for infra file):
- pool_definition:
  - reserved: size=48 GPUs, preemption=false, billing=committed_rate
  - shoulder: size=12 GPUs, preemption=true (eviction only after ephemeral drained), billing=committed_rate (eligible for credit)
  - ephemeral: size=6 GPUs, preemption=true, ttl=30m, billing=on_demand_rate + 15%

- eviction_policy:
  1) drain ephemeral pods with 90s terminationGracePeriod and retry routed to fallback endpoint (warm-smaller-model)
  2) if ephemeral insufficient and traffic > 95th percentile for 10m, promote shoulder for 30m window
  3) reserved used only if shoulder exhausted for > 15m and we hit > 80% utilization on all other pools

- credit_reconciliation_example:
  - month usage: reserved avg util = 78% -> no shoulder credit
  - month usage: reserved avg util = 68% -> shoulder used 1200 GPU-mins -> credit = (shoulder_used_minutes * committed_rate) * 0.25 applied next invoice

Open questions for the docs:
- Do we give a hard cap on shoulder burn per calendar day? (I suggest yes, default 12 GPU-hours/day unless negotiated)
- What metric do we expose via API? (per-minute GPU usage + per-request routed fallback flag)

Please reply with edits and I’ll produce the autoscale JSON and a sample invoice line that procurement can use as an example.

Rohan

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: shoulder/ephemeral carveouts & autoscale policy discussion

Hi Asha — thanks for the quick review and the good questions. We updated the draft policy based on internal feedback; highlights and commitments below. Full draft autoscale JSON and a sample monthly reconciliation table are linked.

Committed changes & commitments:
- Fallback behavior: when ephemeral pods are preempted we will route to a warm-smaller-model (same model family, lower sequence length) with a 90s graceful drain. We will log every fallback event and include a per-request fallback flag in the usage API.
- Eviction guarantees: shoulder will not be preemptively evicted while ephemeral still has running jobs; promotion to shoulder occurs only after ephemeral is drained or TTL expires.
- Credit reconciliation: we will provide a sample invoice line and a per-minute usage API. Credit calculation in sample: shoulder credits are earned when reserved avg util < 70% for the month; credit = 20% of shoulder billed amount for the hours above the credit threshold (example in linked spreadsheet).
- Hard cap: default shoulder burn cap = 12 GPU-hours/day; can be extended by business case.

Action items:
- Rohan: attach autoscale JSON + sample invoice (done) -> https://drive.redwood.com/shared/vl-capacity-plan (see /autoscale/policy.json and /billing/sample-invoice-vl.xlsx)
- Marcus: confirm warm-model routing implementation details by EOD Fri
- Karthik & Ben: provide final credit calc example for procurement to include in term sheet (by Thu COB)
- Asha/Procurement: review the term sheet redlines I attached and send any legal requirements (we'll loop Legal).

If that all sounds ok I’ll push the redlines into the term sheet and schedule a 30-min handoff call with your infra team tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
